en: The Theravāda Vinaya Mahāvibhaṅga:
The Section on Offenses Entailing Expiation (Pācittiyakaṇḍa)
Sappāṇakavagga 69.
The Training Rule on Associating with One Who Has Been Suspended.
At that time, the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
Now at that time, the group-of-six monks, knowing that the monk Ariṭṭha was speaking in such a manner,
had not acted in accordance with the Dhamma, and had not relinquished that view, nevertheless ate together with him, lived together with him,
and even shared a sleeping place with him.
Those monks who were of few desires... they complained, grumbled, and spread it about, saying:

“How can the group-of-six monks, knowing that the monk Ariṭṭha speaks thus, has not acted in accordance with the Dhamma, and has not relinquished that view, still eat together with him, live together with him, and even share a sleeping place with him?”... [and so on]...

“Is it true, monks, that you are living together, dwelling together, and even sharing a sleeping place with the monk Ariṭṭha, who speaks thus knowingly, who has not acted in accordance with the Dhamma, and who has not relinquished that view?
“It is true, Blessed One.
The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them... [as before]...

"How indeed, you foolish men, can you eat together with, dwell together with, or even share a sleeping place with the monk Ariṭṭha, knowing him to be one who speaks thus, who has not acted in accordance with the Dhamma,
and who has not relinquished that view? This, foolish men, does not lead to the confidence of those without confidence..."
And furthermore, monks, you should recite this training rule as follows:

“Whichever monk, knowing that another monk speaks in such a way, has not acted in accordance with the Dhamma, and has not relinquished that view, should eat together with him, live together with him, or share a sleeping place with him, it is an offense entailing expiation (pācittiya).
“Whichever monk” means:
Whoever such as this...
[as before] ...is called a "bhikkhu"... [as before] ...this is what is intended by the term "bhikkhu" in this context.
"Knows" means either he knows it himself, or others inform him of it, or he informs [others] himself.
"Speaking thus" means—

"One who says, 'As I understand the Dhamma taught by the Blessed One, those things called "obstructive states" by the Blessed One are not actually sufficient to be an obstruction for one who indulges in them,'" is one who has not acted in accordance with the Dhamma;
he is suspended and not reinstated.
"Together with one who has not relinquished that view" means together with one who has not relinquished this view.
"Should eat together" means...
“Enjoyment” means two kinds of enjoyment: material enjoyment and Dhamma enjoyment.
Material enjoyment means that one either gives or receives material goods; there is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).
Regarding "Dhammasambhoga":
whether one recites or causes another to recite; whether one recites or causes another to recite by the line; for every line, there is an offense of *pācittiya*.
Whether one recites or causes another to recite by the syllable; for every syllable, there is an offense of *pācittiya*.
"Should live together with" means:
if one performs the Uposatha, the Pavāraṇā, or a formal act of the Saṅgha (saṅghakamma) together with one who has been suspended, there is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).
"Or should share a sleeping place with him" means: [if one does so].
If a suspended monk lies down where he is already covered by a single roof and a regular monk lies down, there is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).
If a regular monk lies down where a suspended monk is already lying down, there is an offense of expiation.
Or if both lie down together, there is an offense of expiation.
Having risen again and again, they lie down; there is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).
If one associates with, lives together with, or shares a sleeping place with one who has been suspended, perceiving that person as suspended, there is an offense of expiation.
If one associates with, lives together with, or shares a sleeping place with one who has been suspended, being uncertain of it, there is an offense of wrongdoing (dukkaṭa).
If one shares a meal with, lives together with, or sleeps in the same place as one who has been suspended, while perceiving that person as not suspended, there is no offense.
If one perceives a person who is not suspended as suspended, there is an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa).
If one is in doubt regarding a person who is not suspended, there is an offense of wrong-doing.
If he is one who has been suspended and he perceives him as such, there is no offense.
There is no offense if he knows: "He has been suspended."
He knows that one who was suspended has been reintegrated;
he knows that one has relinquished that view;
[the case of] one who is insane...
"For one who is a first offender":
the ninth training rule concerning associating with those who have been suspended is finished.
